S001-hmrc-refund-text.title: HMRC says you're owed a tax refund. Would you tap it? #shorts
S001-hmrc-refund-text.desc:
HMRC never tells you about a tax refund by text or email. Real refunds show up in your HMRC account or are paid automatically.
Forward it to 60599 (HMRC) or 7726 (free, your mobile network), then delete it.

S002-hi-mum-whatsapp.title: 'Hi Mum, this is my new number.' Dodgy or not? #shorts
S002-hi-mum-whatsapp.desc:
The 'Hi Mum' scam: a stranger poses as your child on a new number and asks for money. Always call them on the number you already have.
If you sent money, call your bank straight away (159) and report it to Action Fraud.

S003-card-alert-reply-y-n.title: Your bank asks you to reply Y or N. Real or scam? #shorts
S003-card-alert-reply-y-n.desc:
Genuine card fraud alerts from UK banks ask you to reply Y or N only. They never include a link or ask for your PIN, password or codes.
If in doubt, check your banking app or dial 159 to reach your bank safely.
